## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

{"status": "ok", "filepath": "rich/rule.py", "content": "from typing import Union

from .align import AlignMethod
from .cells import cell_len, set_cell_size
from .console import Console, ConsoleOptions, RenderResult
from .jupyter import JupyterMixin
from .measure import Measurement
from .style import Style
from .text import Text


class Rule(JupyterMixin):
    """A console renderable to draw a horizontal rule (line).

    Args:
        title (Union[str, Text], optional): Text to render in the rule. Defaults to "".
        characters (str, optional): Character(s) used to draw the line. Defaults to "─".
        style (StyleType, optional): Style of Rule. Defaults to "rule.line".
        end (str, optional): Character at end of Rule. defaults to "\\\\n"
        align (str, optional): How to align the title, one of "left", "center", or "right". Defaults to "center".
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        title: Union[str, Text] = "",
        *,
        characters: str = "─",
        style: Union[str, Style] = "rule.line",
        end: str = "\n",
        align: AlignMethod = "center",
    ) -> None:
        if cell_len(characters) < 1:
            raise ValueError(
                "'characters' argument must have a cell width of at least 1"
            )
        if align not in ("left", "center", "right"):
            raise ValueError(
                f'invalid value for align, expected "left", "center", "right" (not {align!r})'
            )
        self.title = title
        self.characters = characters
        self.style = style
        self.end = end
        self.align = align

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Rule({self.title!r}, {self.characters!r})"

    def __rich_console__(
        self, console: Console, options: ConsoleOptions
    ) -> RenderResult:
        width = options.max_width

        characters = (
            "-"
            if (options.ascii_only and not self.characters.isascii())
            else self.characters
        )

        chars_len = cell_len(characters)
        if not self.title:
            yield self._rule_line(chars_len, width)
            return

        if isinstance(self.title, Text):
            title_text = self.title
        else:
            title_text = console.render_str(self.title, style="rule.text")

        title_text.plain = title_text.plain.replace("\n", " ")
        title_text.expand_tabs()

        required_space = 4 if self.align == "center" else 2
        truncate_width = max(0, width - required_space)
        if not truncate_width:
            yield self._rule_line(chars_len, width)
            return

        rule_text = Text(end=self.end)
        if self.align == "center":
            title_text.truncate(truncate_width, overflow="ellipsis")
            side_width = (width - cell_len(title_text.plain)) // 2
            left = Text(characters * (side_width // chars_len + 1))
            left.truncate(side_width - 1)
            right_length = width - cell_len(left.plain) - cell_len(title_text.plain)
            right = Text(characters * (side_width // chars_len + 1))
            right.truncate(right_length)
            rule_text.append(left.plain + " ", self.style)
            rule_text.append(title_text)
            rule_text.append(" " + right.plain, self.style)
        elif self.align == "left":
            title_text.truncate(truncate_width, overflow="ellipsis")
            rule_text.append(title_text)
            rule_text.append(" ")
            rule_text.append(characters * (width - rule_text.cell_len), self.style)
        elif self.align == "right":
            title_text.truncate(truncate_width, overflow="ellipsis")
            rule_text.append(characters * (width - title_text.cell_len - 1), self.style)
            rule_text.append(" ")
            rule_text.append(title_text)

        rule_text.plain = set_cell_size(rule_text.plain, width)
        yield rule_text

    def _rule_line(self, chars_len: int, width: int) -> Text:
        rule_text = Text(self.characters * ((width // chars_len) + 1), self.style)
        rule_text.truncate(width)
        rule_text.plain = set_cell_size(rule_text.plain, width)
        return rule_text

    def __rich_measure__(
        self, console: Console, options: ConsoleOptions
    ) -> Measurement:
        return Measurement(1, 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    import sys

    from rich.console import Console

    try:
        text = sys.argv[1]
    except IndexError:
        text = "Hello, World"
    console = Console()
    console.print(Rule(title=text))

    console = Console()
    console.print(Rule("foo"), width=4)", "start_line": 1, "end_line": 130, "total_lines": 130, "is_truncated": false}
